org.roles.desc.OWNER: Everything, including deleting the organization and changing another owner.
org.roles.desc.ADMIN: Everything except deleting the organization or touching an owner.
org.roles.desc.DEVELOPER: Deploy, terminal, files, databases, backups. No membership or plan changes.
org.roles.desc.VIEWER: Read only: overview, logs and metrics. No terminal and no file manager.
org.quota.consequence.DOMAIN: You cannot point another hostname at a service.
org.quota.consequence.VOLUME_BYTES: You cannot attach or grow a volume.
org.quota.consequence.MEMORY_BYTES: You cannot give a service more memory.
org.quota.consequence.CPU_MILLICORES: You cannot give a service more CPU.
org.quota.consequence.BACKUP_BYTES: The next snapshot will be refused.
org.quota.consequence.RESTORE_POINT: The oldest snapshot has to go before another is taken.
org.quota.consequence.DEPLOYMENTS_PER_DA: Deploys are paused until the rolling day moves on.
org.quota.source.unsetHint: Not set on this plan, so nothing is allowed. Ask an operator to set it.
org.quota.zeroCountHint: Zero means the tenant may not have any at all.
org.list.title: Organizations
org.list.description: Each one has its own members, its own plan and its own limits. Projects live inside them.
org.list.emptyInvitedTitle: Not a member of anything yet
org.list.emptyInvitedDesc: Join one of the invitations above, or open an organization of your own - a project has to live inside one.
org.list.emptyDesc: An organization owns the projects, the members and the plan. Open one and the first project can go straight in it.
org.row.suspendedDefaultReason: Suspended by an operator. Nothing new can be created until it is resumed.
org.create.title: New organization
org.create.description: A tenant of its own: separate members, separate plan, separate limits.
org.create.name: Name
org.create.noSelectablePlansHint: No plan is selectable right now. The default one is used, and an operator can move you later.
org.create.plansHint: An operator can move the organization to another plan afterwards.
org.overview.defaultDescription: What this organization is allowed, and who is in it.
org.overview.suspendedFallbackReason: An operator suspended it. No reason was recorded on the record.
org.overview.suspendedNotice: Everything already running keeps running. Nothing new can be created until an operator resumes it.
org.overview.noPlan: This organization is not on a plan, which means every limit below is zero and nothing new can be created. An operator has to assign one - it is not something that can be fixed from here.
org.overview.planFooter: Changing tier is an operator decision. Ask, and they can move the organization or grant an exception on a single limit without moving it.
org.overview.limitsDescription: What the plan allows, and what is used against it right now.

org.overview.peopleDesc.one: 1 person has access to everything in this organization.
org.overview.peopleDesc.other: {count} people have access to everything in this organization.

org.overview.peopleNote: A member's role decides what they may do in every project here, not in one of them. Fine-grained per-project access is deliberately not a thing: a permission model nobody can hold in their head is a permission model that gets granted wide and left.
org.members.title: Members
org.members.description: A role applies to every project in this organization. There is no per-project access, on purpose: a permission model nobody can hold in their head gets granted wide and left.
org.members.singleOwnerWarning: There is one owner. If that account is lost, nobody can invite anybody, change a role or move this organization onto another plan - promote a second one.
org.members.readOnlyNotice: Inviting people and changing roles is an owner or admin decision, so those controls are off for you. You can still see who has access.
org.members.peoplePending: {total} in total, {pending} still to answer their invitation.
org.members.emptyDesc: That is unusual - an organization normally keeps its owner. Invite somebody with an account on this installation and they will appear here as soon as they are asked.
org.invite.title: Invite somebody
org.invite.description: They keep their own account and appear here as invited until they accept.
org.invite.seatsFull: Every seat on the plan is taken: {quota}. Remove somebody, or ask an operator for a larger plan or an exception.
org.invite.seatsRemaining: {quota} used, including invitations that have not been answered.
org.invite.emailHint: They need an account on this installation already - there is no public sign-up, so an operator creates it.
org.memberDialog.descInvited: {name} has been invited as {role} and has not answered yet.
org.memberDialog.confirmLeaveBody: You lose access to every project in it. Somebody still inside would have to invite you back.
org.memberDialog.confirmRemoveBody: They lose access to every project in this organization straight away. Nothing they built is deleted.
org.memberDialog.explainLastOwnerSelf: You are the last owner. Make somebody else an owner before you change your role or leave - otherwise nobody could administer this organization.
org.memberDialog.explainLastOwnerOther: This is the last owner, so they cannot be demoted or removed. Make somebody else an owner first.
org.memberDialog.explainReachingPastSelf: Only an owner can change or remove another owner. Ask one of them, or ask to be made an owner yourself.
org.memberDialog.explainNotAdmin: Changing roles is an owner or admin decision, so the picker is off for you. Leaving is your own to make.
org.memberDialog.explainNotOwner: An admin can move people between admin, developer and viewer. Making somebody an owner is an owner’s decision.
org.memberDialog.explainDefault: An organization always keeps at least one owner, so the last one cannot be demoted or removed.
org.adminTenants.title: Tenants
org.adminTenants.description: Every organization on this installation, which plan it is on and whether it is suspended.
org.adminTenants.emptyQueryDesc: No tenant's name or address contains “{query}”. Clear the filter to see all {total}.
org.adminTenants.emptyDesc: Nobody has opened one. A customer creates their own from the Organizations screen; there is no operator form for it, because the person who opens a tenant has to end up owning it.
org.adminDetail.suspendedFallbackReason: No reason was recorded on the record.
org.adminDetail.limitsDesc: The plan's numbers, with any exception below already applied.
org.adminDetail.peopleNoOwners: Nobody here owns this organization, which should not happen - it is worth looking at.
org.adminDetail.peopleDesc: {access} with access, {owners} {ownerWord}. Members are managed by the owners, not from here.
org.adminDetail.peopleEmpty: No member rows at all. The tenant exists and nobody can reach it.
org.tenantPlan.title: Plan
org.tenantPlan.descNoPlan: This tenant is not on a plan, so every limit is zero.
org.tenantPlan.hint: Only selectable tiers are offered, plus whichever one this tenant is on.
org.tenantPlan.note: Moving changes what is allowed from now on. Nothing is deleted and nothing is stopped: a tenant that ends up over a limit keeps what it has and cannot create more until it is back under.
org.tenantStatus.fallbackReason: No reason was recorded on the record.
org.tenantStatus.customerViewNotice: The customer sees this sentence on their organization screen. Resuming clears it and lets them create things again straight away.
org.tenantStatus.suspendDesc: Stops this tenant creating anything new. Nothing already running is touched.
org.tenantStatus.reasonHint: Required, and shown to the customer. Say what would lift it - an unpaid invoice, an abuse report, a migration in progress.
org.tenantStatus.confirmBody: They cannot create projects, services, domains, databases, backups or invitations until this is lifted. Everything already running keeps running, and the reason you wrote is shown to them.
org.overrides.title: Exceptions
org.overrides.description: Limits that apply to this organization instead of its plan's.
org.overrides.emptyDesc: Every limit comes from the plan. Grant one to raise - or lower - a single resource for this tenant without moving them onto a different tier.
org.overrides.confirmBody: This organization goes back to whatever its plan allows on the next request it makes. Nothing it has already created is removed.
org.grantOverride.title: Grant an exception
org.grantOverride.desc: Replaces one limit for this organization only. The plan is left alone.
org.grantOverride.hintNotInForce: Nothing is in force for this resource yet.
org.grantOverride.reasonHint: Kept on the exception and in the audit trail. Whoever finds this in six months is you.
org.grantOverride.expiresHint: Leave it empty for an exception that stands until it is revoked.
org.plans.title: Plans
org.plans.description: What an organization is allowed. Every tenant is on exactly one, and exceptions are granted per tenant.
org.plans.noDefaultDesc: Opening an organization is refused while this is true, because a tenant on no plan has every limit at zero. Make one of the tiers below the default.
org.plans.emptyDesc: Nothing can be created on this installation until there is one: an organization needs a plan, and a plan is what says how many projects, services and gigabytes it may have. Make one, set its limits, and mark it as the default.
org.plans.confirmRetireBody: It stops being offered to new organizations. Everyone already on it stays on it with exactly the limits they have now, and you can bring it back at any time.
org.planDetail.fallbackDesc: The {code} tier and the thirteen numbers on it.

org.planDetail.unsetAlertTitle.one: One limit has never been set

org.planDetail.unsetAlertDesc: An unset limit is zero, so every one of them refuses the customer's first attempt. They are marked below.
org.planDetail.retiredNotice: Retired: no new organization can be opened on it and no tenant can be moved onto it. The {count} already here are unaffected.

org.planDetail.limitsDesc.one: Applies to every organization on this tier - 1 of them, except where an exception has been granted.
org.planDetail.limitsDesc.other: Applies to every organization on this tier - {count} of them, except where an exception has been granted.
org.planDetail.limitsDesc.zero: Applies to every organization on this tier, except where an exception has been granted.

org.planDetail.confirmRetireBody: It stops being offered to new organizations. The {count} already on it stay on it, unchanged.
org.createPlan.title: New plan
org.createPlan.desc: Every limit starts at zero, so set them before anybody is moved onto it.
org.createPlan.codeHint: Short, stable, and what appears in audit lines. It is not shown to customers as a title.
org.createPlan.name: Name
org.createPlan.nameHint: What the customer sees on their organization screen.
org.createPlan.descHint: Optional. One line about who this tier is for.
org.planLimit.descUnset: Never set on this plan, so it is zero: nothing of this kind is allowed at all.
org.planLimit.atZero: At zero: {consequence} A tenant already over the new number keeps what it has and cannot add more.
org.planLimit.scopeNote: This applies to every organization on the tier, except the ones holding an exception for this resource.
